_comment: Abscess, sinus and fistula. Subtitle: Examination of a sinus. Almost every bedside finding is an emphasis overlay on a shared surgery skill; the disease owns only the mechanism (why tracks persist), the abscess spectrum, the workup, the diagnosis statement and the management principles.
name: Abscess, sinus and fistula
oneLine: A discharging track examined to its keeper, and the abscesses that start one

chapters.title: Basics
chapters.blurb: A blind track, a communicating track, and a collection of pus

chapters.title: Patient particulars
chapters.blurb: Age, work and home set the likely keeper before the track is seen

skill.particulars.demographics.expect: Record occupation with what the work does to the body: a barefoot field worker collects thorn pricks and minor leg trauma, a tailor sitting long hours nurses a natal cleft sinus, a health worker may carry a stitch sinus from a past operation. Note who gives the history, since operative details from years ago are often approximate.

chapters.title: History of presenting illness
chapters.blurb: How long it discharges, what comes out, and what started it

skill.hx.chief_complaints.expect: Expect the chief complaint in discharge words: a hole that leaks, with duration in months, not days. Fix the tempo first, since an acute abscess story runs in days while a sinus story runs in months to years.

skill.hx.surg.sinus_fistula.expect: Expect an antecedent abscess that burst or was incised, then a track that never closed. Ask what the discharge contains: pus alone, bony particles that grit between the fingers, sulphur granules, hair, or faeces, flatus, urine or bile that would make it a fistula and not a sinus.

chapters.title: Past, personal, drug and family history
chapters.blurb: The keepers live in the past history

chapters.title: General examination
chapters.blurb: Fever, nutrition and the diabetic behind the track

skill.gen.appearance.expect: Look for the two states of the patient: quiet chronic discharge with a well patient, or an active flare with a toxic, febrile patient guarding a red limb. Pallor from chronic disease anaemia and pedal oedema from undernutrition both slow healing and must be recorded.

skill.gen.vitals.expect: Expect normal vitals in a quiet chronic sinus. Fever with tachycardia marks an active flare or spreading cellulitis and changes the urgency, while hypotension with a rapidly spreading red painful limb is a necrotising emergency, not a sinus to examine at leisure.

skill.gen.surg.survey.expect: Survey for the keepers at a glance: glycosuria habitus and acanthosis of diabetes, cervical or axillary scars of old tuberculous nodes, clubbing of chronic suppuration, and the footwear and foot care of a leg sinus patient.

chapters.title: Examination of the sinus
chapters.blurb: Number, site, opening, track, probe and nodes

skill.exam.surg.sinus_fistula_inspect.expect: Expect a single opening fixed to deep tissue over the middle third of the shin, with sprouting granulation at its mouth pointing to dead bone beneath. Multiple openings would swing you toward actinomycosis or hidradenitis, and a puckered bluish undermined edge toward tuberculosis.

skill.exam.surg.sinus_fistula_palpate.expect: Expect the track fixed to irregular, thickened, tender tibia with a firm fibrous wall along its course. Mobility over deep structures would argue against an osteomyelitic origin, and a nearby lump would raise tuberculous nodes.

skill.exam.surg.sinus_probing.expect: Expect the probe to pass a few centimetres along the tibial surface and strike a hard, gritty, moveable sequestrum at the depth of the track. Fresh pus welling on withdrawal confirms an undrained deep pool. Defer probing during an active flare with spreading cellulitis and fever: probe gently under senior cover only once the flare settles, with antibiotics on board.

skill.exam.surg.chronic_osteomyelitis.expect: Expect the full bone signature around the sinus: broadened irregular tibia, thickening, tenderness, wasting of the calf from disuse, and sometimes shortening or deformity from the old fracture and its fixation.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.expect: Expect soft, tender, palpable inguinal nodes in the active flare that settle as it resolves. Matted, rubbery or cold nodes would raise tuberculosis or lymphoma instead of simple drainage.

stations.title: Examine this discharging sinus
stations.task: This 34 year old man has a discharging sinus over his left shin for eighteen months. The leg is currently hot, red and febrile, so do not probe the track today; examine the sinus, present your findings, and state when and how you would examine it with a probe.
examinerQuestions: You found sprouting granulation at the mouth with the track fixed to bone. What does that combination tell you?
Your probe strikes a hard, gritty, moveable sequestrum. What is it, and what operation does it mandate?
When would you refuse to probe a sinus, and what would you do instead?

stations.title: Take a history from a discharging sinus
stations.task: This 34 year old man has had a discharging opening over his shin for over a year. Take a focused history in six minutes and be ready to name the likely keeper of the track.
examinerQuestions: What in his story separates a sinus from a fistula?
Name three keepers your history specifically excluded, and how.
What single past detail would make tuberculosis your leading keeper?

skill.reasoning.sinus.basics.title: What a sinus, a fistula and an abscess are
skill.reasoning.sinus.basics.oneLine: A blind track, a communicating track, and a walled pool of pus
skill.reasoning.sinus.basics.why: Students mix the three words and then mismanage all three conditions. A blind track can be left to close once its keeper is removed, a communicating track never closes while bowel contents or urine run through it, and a tense pool of pus needs release before anything else. The name decides the operation.

teach.heading: Three words, three anatomies
teach.body:
A sinus is a blind track from an epithelial surface down into the tissues, often to a cavity, and it ends blindly. A fistula is an abnormal communicating track between two epithelial surfaces: skin to bowel, skin to bladder, or bowel to bowel.

An abscess is a localised collection of pus within a tissue, walled by inflammation. The three connect in time: an abscess that bursts or is drained leaves a sinus, and an abscess of a viscus that bursts outward leaves a fistula.

teach.heading: How the track is lined
teach.body:
Both tracks are first lined by granulation tissue, which later epithelialises from either end. Once the lining is complete skin, the track is a skin tube and no dressing will close it: it needs excision or its cause removed.

This is why duration matters. A track of weeks may still collapse and heal; a track of months with a smooth epithelial lining will not, and promising dressings alone wastes the patient's season.

teach.heading: Classify first, then examine
points: Sinuses: congenital from failed fusion, traumatic around retained foreign material, inflammatory from bone, node or bowel disease, neoplastic from a degenerating growth, and the pilonidal sinus of the natal cleft.
Fistulae: congenital from failed closure, traumatic after operation or injury to a viscus, inflammatory where a visceral abscess bursts outward, and malignant where a cancer eats into a neighbour.
Position alone often names the congenital ones: the root of the helix, the lower third of the neck before the sternomastoid, and the midline behind the anus.
A deep neck abscess shows the same logic in reverse: pus in the plane between pharynx and spine threatens the airway first, and only then becomes a track question.

probes.q: What is the anatomical difference between a sinus and a fistula?
probes.a: A sinus is a blind track from a surface into the tissues with no second opening, while a fistula is a communicating track between two epithelial surfaces.

probes.q: Why does an old epithelialised track refuse to heal with dressings?
probes.a: Because its wall has become lined skin, a complete tube that cannot stick together, so only excision or removal of its cause will close it.

probes.q: A neck swelling bursts and discharges for a year. Why do you ask first whether the opening was present since birth?
probes.a: Because a congenital track such as a branchial fistula never closes on its own and needs elective excision, while an acquired inflammatory track may close once its keeper is treated.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.sinus.abscess.title: The abscess spectrum: hot, blood borne and cold
skill.reasoning.sinus.abscess.oneLine: Pyogenic, pyaemic and cold abscesses, with boil and carbuncle
skill.reasoning.sinus.abscess.why: Not every collection of pus behaves hot. A pyogenic abscess shouts with throbbing pain and brawny oedema, blood borne abscesses hide deep without local signs while the patient burns with rigors, and a cold abscess grows silently for months. Treating a cold abscess as a hot one, by incising it like any boil, seeds a sinus that never closes.

teach.heading: The common hot abscess
teach.body:
The pyogenic abscess follows cellulitis or node infection, seeded directly through a wound, from a neighbouring focus, or by blood or lymph. The part turns red, hot and tender, pain turns throbbing once pus forms, and brawny oedema pits on pressure.

Fluctuation is late and sometimes absent, as in the parotid, so waiting for it before draining wastes days. Throbbing pain with brawny induration is enough to act on.

teach.heading: Blood borne abscesses hide
teach.body:
Pyaemic abscesses are multiple, appearing together or in crops after one is incised, because infected emboli lodge in many sites at once. They favour deep planes and show none of the classic heat and pointing of a surface abscess.

The constitutional storm gives them away: high fever with rigor and profound toxaemia out of proportion to any local sign. Here the treatment is the bloodstream and the source, not the knife on any single lump.

teach.heading: Cold abscesses and the diabetic pair
points: A cold abscess is almost always tuberculous, from nodes, spine, ribs or joints, and it is cold because caseation replaces acute inflammation: no heat, no brawny oedema, no tenderness.
Favour neck, axilla, loin, back and chest wall, tracking along fascial planes far from its bony origin, and it limits spine movement when the spine is the source.

A boil is a hair follicle infection that points, bursts greenish slough, and heals, while a carbuncle is infective gangrene of subcutaneous tissue with sieve like openings, classically on the nape of a diabetic man past forty.
Recurrent boils and carbuncles demand a sugar check, and a cold abscess demands antitubercular treatment, never a simple incision.

probes.q: How does a cold abscess differ from a pyogenic one on examination?
probes.a: It is cold and non tender, without heat, brawny oedema or throbbing pain, because caseation replaces acute inflammation.

probes.q: Why is incising a cold abscess like a boil a serious error?
probes.a: Because the tuberculous lining will not granulate and close, so the incision becomes a chronic discharging sinus, and the underlying bony or nodal disease goes untreated.

probes.q: A diabetic man has a sieve like discharging swelling on his nape with ashy slough. What is it, and what two things does it oblige?
probes.a: A carbuncle, which obliges sugar control alongside wide care of the sloughing area, since poor resistance lets it burrow to muscle or bone.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.sinus.signs.title: Reading the sinus: opening, discharge, track and nodes
skill.reasoning.sinus.signs.oneLine: One keeper explains every local sign
skill.reasoning.sinus.signs.why: The opening, the discharge, the feel of the track and the state of the nodes all point at the same keeper, and the student who reads them together names the cause before any film. Read separately they are just a leaking hole with a sore around it.

teach.heading: The opening confesses
teach.body:
Sprouting exuberant granulation at the mouth means a foreign body or dead bone waits below: sequestrum, suture, mesh, bullet or tube. A wide mouth with a thin blue undermined edge means tuberculosis, and a raised rolled or everted margin warns of malignant change.

Number matters as much as shape. Multiplicity belongs to actinomycosis, hidradenitis and Crohn disease of the anorectum, while a solitary track fixed to bone belongs to osteomyelitis.

teach.heading: The discharge and the probe
teach.body:
Pus alone is pyogenic osteomyelitis, bony grit is dead bone, serosanguineous fluid is tuberculous, and sulphur granules are actinomycosis. Faeces, flatus, urine or bile reclassify the case as a fistula on the spot.

The probe reports direction and depth, gritty moveable sequestrum at the bottom, communication with a viscus, and fresh pus welling on withdrawal. Probe gently and never force, and never probe a suspected vascular or parotid track without senior cover.

teach.heading: Nodes and the neighbourhood
points: Draining nodes are never skipped: tender and soft in a flare, matted and rubbery in tuberculosis, hard and fixed when a chronic sinus turns malignant.
Fixation to irregular thickened tender bone seals an osteomyelitic origin, while a nearby doughy lump points to nodal disease.
Surrounding dermatitis with pigmentation favours Crohn disease and actinomycosis, and digested excoriated skin proves a small bowel leak.
Examine the system behind the site: spine, ribs and kidneys for a loin sinus, chest for an empyema sinus, mouth and anorectum with a scope where indicated.

probes.q: What does sprouting granulation tissue at a sinus mouth signify?
probes.a: A foreign body or dead bone in the depth, such as a sequestrum, retained suture, mesh or drainage tube.

probes.q: Contrast a tuberculous sinus opening with a pyogenic one.
probes.a: The tuberculous opening is wide with a thin blue undermined margin and serosanguineous discharge, while the pyogenic one pours pus and may sprout granulation over a palpable bony irregularity.

probes.q: A chronic sinus edge turns raised and everted. What has happened, and what now?
probes.a: Malignant change, a Marjolin ulcer, so the edge needs biopsy and the lesion needs oncologic assessment rather than another course of dressings.

sources.source: Browse's Introduction to the Symptoms and Signs of Surgical Disease

skill.reasoning.sinus.differential.title: Differential diagnosis of a discharging track
skill.reasoning.sinus.differential.oneLine: Site writes half the list; the discharge writes the rest
skill.reasoning.sinus.differential.why: A discharging track has a short list, but the wrong pick changes the operation: laying open a Crohn fistula as if it were simple, or incising a cold abscess as if it were a boil, harms the patient for months. Site first, discharge second, and the keepers last.

teach.heading: Let the site speak first
teach.body:
Some positions are diagnoses: helix root for preauricular sinus, lower neck before the sternomastoid for branchial fistula, midline natal cleft for pilonidal sinus, and perianal clock positions for fistula in ano with its Goodsall rule.

A groin sinus tracks from hip or spine, a loin sinus from spine, ribs or kidney, a jaw sinus from dental or bony disease, and a scar sinus from stitch, mesh or dead bone. Write the site before anything else and half the list is already ordered.

teach.heading: Then the discharge and the course
teach.body:
Bony particles mean osteomyelitis, sulphur granules mean actinomycosis, serosanguineous fluid with a blue undermined edge means tuberculosis, and bowel contents or urine mean fistula. Intermittent discharge with recurrent painful swelling means the mouth keeps sealing over a retained pool.

An infected sebaceous cyst has a punctum and a doughy past, hidradenitis has multiple axillary or groin pits, and a pilonidal sinus holds hair in midline pits. Each has a texture and a tempo of its own.

teach.heading: The dangerous and the systemic mimics
points: Tuberculous osteomyelitis and nodal disease mimic pyogenic tracks exactly until the discharge, the edge and the contact history are weighed.
Crohn disease explains multiple complex perianal fistulae in a young patient with diarrhoea, mouth ulcers and weight loss, and changes fistulotomy into bowel workup.
A chronic sinus or scar that turns raised and everted is Marjolin change until biopsy says otherwise, and an ulcer with sinus needs the same suspicion.
Necrotising fasciitis is the red flag inside an acute flare: pain beyond the redness, dusky skin, crepitus and toxicity demand theatre, not dressings.

probes.q: Name four site diagnoses of discharging tracks.
probes.a: Preauricular sinus at the helix, branchial fistula in the lower neck, pilonidal sinus in the natal cleft, and fistula in ano at the anal verge.

probes.q: What features separate a tuberculous track from a pyogenic one?
probes.a: An insidious cold course, a wide blue undermined edge, serosanguineous discharge, matted nodes or a spinal focus, and a household contact history.

probes.q: Multiple complex perianal fistulae in a young man with chronic diarrhoea. What must precede any operation?
probes.a: Bowel assessment for Crohn disease with colonoscopy, since laying open these fistulae as simple ones risks incontinence without treating the bowel.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.investigation.sinus.workup.title: Workup of a discharging track
skill.investigation.sinus.workup.oneLine: Discharge, bone, track and sugar, in that order
skill.investigation.sinus.workup.why: Every test here answers one question: what keeps the track open. Discharge study names the organism, the radiograph finds dead bone, the dye study maps the track, and sugar testing finds the diabetic behind recurrent sepsis. A test that does not name a keeper is a delay.

teach.heading: Start with the discharge itself
teach.body:
Examine the discharge macroscopically for pus, blood staining, bony grit, hair and sulphur granules, then send it for microscopy, Gram stain, culture with sensitivity, and acid fast staining where tuberculosis is possible.

Collect pus before antibiotics where feasible, and from the depth rather than the skin edge, since surface swabs grow colonisers. Blood culture joins in during a febrile flare, and a full blood count with inflammatory markers grades the activity.

teach.heading: Image the bone and map the track
teach.body:
A plain radiograph of the part shows sequestrum, involucrum, cloacae and the old fracture or implant behind an osteomyelitic sinus. Where the track is complex, a sinogram or fistulogram with radio opaque dye outlines its course and any visceral communication.

Cross sectional imaging stages the deep extent: ultrasound for a superficial pool, computed tomography for bone detail and mediastinal spread in neck disease, and magnetic resonance for fistula in ano and spinal involvement.

teach.heading: Dye tests, systemic tests and biopsy
points: Methylene blue through a catheter confirms a vesicovaginal fistula when colour appears in the vagina, charcoal in food confirms an upper gut fistula, and a coloured urinary drug confirms a urinary leak.

Test sugar and renal function in every recurrent or non healing track, test HIV where risk or severity is unexplained, and work up tuberculosis with chest film, nodal or spine imaging and tissue diagnosis.
Biopsy any raised, rolled or everted edge, since Marjolin change hides in old sinuses and scars.
In a neck swelling with stridor or drooling, the airway comes before every test on this list.

probes.q: What does a plain radiograph show in an osteomyelitic sinus?
probes.a: A dense sequestrum sitting in an involucrum, with cloacae through which pus reaches the skin, plus the old fracture line or implant.

probes.q: Why must pus come from the depth before antibiotics, not as a surface swab later?
probes.a: Because surface swabs grow skin colonisers while the true pathogen lives in the deep pool, and antibiotics sterilise the culture without sterilising the nidus.

probes.q: Vaginal leakage is suspected after pelvic surgery. How do you confirm a vesicovaginal fistula at the bedside?
probes.a: Pass sterilised methylene blue through a catheter into the bladder; blue staining in the vagina confirms the communication.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.reasoning.sinus.diagnosis.title: The diagnostic statement and its red flags
skill.reasoning.sinus.diagnosis.oneLine: Name the track, the keeper, the state and the threat
skill.reasoning.sinus.diagnosis.why: A diagnosis of sinus alone books no operation and warns of no danger. The statement must name whether it is blind or communicating, what keeps it open, whether it is quiet or flaring, and what threatens the patient now, because each clause orders a different next step.

teach.heading: Four clauses, one diagnosis
teach.body:
First the anatomy: single or multiple, exact site, sinus or fistula with what leaks. Second the keeper: sequestrum, retained mesh or suture, tuberculosis, Crohn disease, pilonidal disease, or keeper unknown pending workup.

Third the state: quiet chronic discharge or active flare with fever and cellulitis. Fourth the threat: none beyond the track, or spreading infection, airway risk in neck disease, or suspected malignant change.

teach.heading: Red flags that overrule the routine
points: Stridor, drooling or respiratory distress in neck swelling means airway first, with intubation and rarely tracheostomy before any track examination.
Rapidly spreading pain beyond redness, dusky skin, crepitus or toxicity means necrotising infection and immediate surgical review.
Chest pain with sepsis from neck or chest disease means descending mediastinitis until imaging excludes it.
Neurological signs with a back sinus mean spinal involvement, and a raised everted edge means biopsy before any excision plan.

teach.heading: Referral thresholds from a primary setting
teach.body:
A quiet single sinus with a visible keeper and a cooperative patient can be worked up at the district hospital with radiograph, culture and sugar testing. Multiple, recurrent, perianal complex, spinal, urinary or bowel leaking tracks need a surgical centre with imaging and scope support.

Any red flag, any suspected malignancy, and any child with neck swelling and noisy breathing go the same day. Write the keeper you suspect on the referral, so the centre images the right thing first.

probes.q: What four clauses make a complete sinus diagnosis?
probes.a: The anatomy of the track, the keeper that holds it open, the current state of quiet or flare, and any red flag threat.

probes.q: A child has neck swelling with drooling and stridor. What outranks the sinus workup?
probes.a: The airway: secure it with intubation and rarely tracheostomy first, since a deep neck abscess obstructs before it ever becomes a track.

probes.q: When does a sinus seen at a primary centre need same day referral?
probes.a: With any red flag such as stridor, spreading toxicity or suspected mediastinitis, any suspected malignant edge, any spinal or complex perianal track, and any noisy breathing child with neck swelling.

skill.treatment.sinus.management.title: Managing abscess, sinus and fistula
skill.treatment.sinus.management.oneLine: Remove the keeper, drain the pool, rest the part
skill.treatment.sinus.management.why: Dressings never cured a kept track, and antibiotics never sterilised dead bone. Cure follows the keeper: take out what should not be there, let pus out downhill, keep the part still, and treat the systemic disease behind it. Everything else is support while that happens.

teach.heading: Abscess first: release and cover
teach.body:
A tense pyogenic abscess needs timely incision and drainage with pus sent for culture, alongside empirical antibiotics covering skin flora and oral anaerobes, later narrowed to the culture report. Support with fluids, analgesia and limb elevation where relevant.

A deep neck abscess adds airway protection as the first step, drainage usually through the mouth in the acute form, and watch for mediastinal spread. A cold tuberculous abscess is never incised like a boil: it needs antitubercular therapy with drainage by needle or an external route that will not seed a chronic sinus.

teach.heading: Sinus next: take the keeper away
teach.body:
Remove sequestrum with saucerisation of the bony bed, retrieve suture, mesh or bullet, and lay the track open or excise it once epithelialised. Establish dependent drainage so no pool reforms, and rest the part: immobilise the limb, regulate bowel rest where indicated, and stop the movement that holds perianal tracks open.

Control sugar tightly in diabetics, correct anaemia and nutrition, and stop smoking counsel at every visit. Review the wound weekly until the discharge dries, and re image where closure stalls.

teach.heading: Fistula and follow up
points: Remember that opening the natural passage heals the abnormal offshoot: relieve the distal obstruction and many low fistulae close without direct attack.
Tuberculous tracks need the full antitubercular course with adherence support under the national programme, and Crohn related tracks need bowel disease control with a colorectal surgeon involved.
Malignant change needs oncologic referral after biopsy, never wider dressings.
Safety net every discharge: return for spreading redness, fever, foul increase, fresh bleeding, or the mouth sealing over with renewed painful swelling.

probes.q: What are the three moves that close a kept sinus?
probes.a: Remove the keeper such as dead bone or retained material, establish dependent drainage of any pool, and rest the part until healed.

probes.q: How does drainage of a cold tuberculous abscess differ from a pyogenic one?
probes.a: It is drained by needle aspiration or an external approach with antitubercular drugs, never by simple incision like a boil, which would seed a chronic sinus.

probes.q: A deep neck abscess patient develops noisy breathing. What is the order of management?
probes.a: Airway first with intubation and rarely tracheostomy, then broad intravenous antibiotics, then transoral drainage of the acute collection with monitoring for mediastinitis.

sources.source: Bailey and Love's Short Practice of Surgery

skill.treatment.sinus.management.dosingNote: This module teaches management at the level of drug class and operative principle. Specific agents, routes and durations must be taken from your current national or institutional guideline and local resistance data at the time of prescribing. CliniX does not prescribe.

cases.title: A cane cutter with a shin that has leaked for eighteen months
cases.opening: Ramesh Mane, 34, walks into the surgical outpatient room with a stick, his left trouser leg cut short and stained. He smells faintly of old dressings. Introduce yourself and take a history.
cases.fallback: I do not understand, doctor. Please ask me in a simpler way.

patient.name: Ramesh Mane
patient.residence: Rural, tin roof house with wife, two children and parents

cues: what brings you here today
what is the main problem
why have you come to hospital
tell me everything from the very beginning
presenting.reply: Doctor, for one and a half years there is a small hole over my left shin that keeps leaking pus. It never dries fully, and for the last week the leg has become painful and red around it with fever.

cues: when did the leak begin
how long has the hole been leaking
how did the discharge start
was the opening there since birth
discharge_onset_course.reply: It began about eighteen months ago, a few weeks after my rod operation wound broke open. It was never there since birth. Since then it leaks almost daily, sometimes less, never fully dry for more than a few days.

cues: describe what comes out of the hole
is the leaking fluid yellow, bloody or watery
does the discharge smell bad
have you seen bony chips in the discharge
discharge_character_detail.reply: Thick yellow pus, foul smelling on bad days, enough to soak a small gauze pad daily. Twice I have seen tiny hard gritty white particles in it, like sand, which the dresser said were bone pieces.

cues: is the leg painful now
describe the character of the leg pain
do you get fever with chills
has the pain become throbbing recently
pain_flare_pattern.reply: Usually only a dull ache. Since last week it throbs, the skin around is red and hot, and I get fever with shivering every evening. Walking now hurts, so I use a stick.

cues: was there an injury before the hole appeared
tell me about the fracture operation
was the wound open at the time of injury
did the operation wound break open
injury_abscess_origin.reply: Two years ago a loaded cart wheel ran over my left leg in the field and the bone came out through the skin. At the district hospital they put a rod inside and stitched it. A month later pus started from the stitch line and the wound opened.

cues: was the swelling cut open anytime
how many operations on this leg
was dead bone removed anytime
what dressings have been applied so far
prior_drainage_procedures.reply: One rod operation two years ago, and one small procedure six months later when they opened the swelling and washed it. No one said anything about removing dead bone. Since then only gauze dressings at the village centre, changed every two or three days.

cues: does the mouth close over at times
does the opening seal followed by swelling
do you get repeated painful swellings
does the leak stop before the pain returns
discharge_interruptions.reply: Yes, two or three times the hole closed for a week and each time the leg swelled up painfully with fever, then it burst open again with a gush of pus. That is when the pain is worst.

cues: does stool or urine leak from the hole
have you passed wind through the opening
is there any bowel content in the discharge
does the leak increase after food or water
fistula_leak_exclusion.reply: No, nothing like stool, urine or wind comes from it, only pus. Eating or passing urine makes no difference to the leak.

cues: can you walk without support
how far can you walk now
have you lost work because of this
is the leg becoming thin from disuse
limb_function_livelihood.reply: I walk with a stick and cannot go beyond the farm boundary. Last cutting season I earned half wages because I could not keep up with the gang. My left calf has become thin, the right leg still does all the work.

cues: anyone at home with prolonged cough
have you had evening fever and night sweats
any gland swellings in the neck earlier
have you taken tuberculosis medicines before
tb_contact_screen.reply: Nobody at home coughs for long or has taken TB medicines. I never had neck glands or evening sweats, only this leg problem with recent fever. My weight is less than two years ago but my appetite is still fair.

cues: do you have sugar disease
any excessive thirst and urination
was your blood sugar ever tested
do you get recurrent boils elsewhere
diabetes_sugar_screen.reply: No sugar disease that I know. I drink normal water and pass urine normally. Once at a camp they pricked my finger and said sugar was normal. I do not get boils anywhere else.

cues: which medicines are you taking now
have you taken steroid tablets anytime
how many antibiotic courses so far
do you apply any native medicine on it
medication_history_detail.reply: Only paracetamol for fever this week. Earlier I took white capsules from the village doctor many times, each time the leak lessened for a while. No steroids, no regular tablets, and no native paste, only clean gauze.

cues: any long diarrhoea with blood or mucus
any mouth ulcers that keep coming
any previous jaundice or joint pains
were you ever told your immunity is low
past_illness_background.reply: My motions are normal, no blood or mucus, no mouth ulcers. No jaundice, no joint pains, no long illness before this leg. Nobody ever said my immunity is low.

cues: do you smoke bidis or cigarettes
do you chew tobacco or gutkha
how often do you drink alcohol
what do you eat on a working day
personal_habits_profile.reply: Two or three bidis a day for ten years, no chewing. Country liquor on festival days only. On working days bhakri, dal, onion and sometimes an egg; meat rarely, milk only for the children.

care_received_so_far.reply: Only the village centre for dressings and the district hospital once for the washout procedure. The doctor there said this hole needs a bigger bone operation and sent me here with a slip.

skill.gen.appearance.finding: Lean adult male, alert and febrile, wincing on left leg movement. Walks with a stick, non weight bearing on the left leg. Mild pallor, no icterus, no pedal oedema, tongue moist.

skill.gen.vitals.finding: Temperature 38.4 C. Pulse 96 per minute, regular, normal volume. Blood pressure 128/84. Respiratory rate 20 per minute. SpO2 98 percent on room air.

skill.exam.surg.sinus_fistula_inspect.finding: Single opening over the middle third of the left shin, 8 mm across, raised on sprouting red granulation tissue. Foul yellow pus wells on pressure around it. Surrounding skin red, warm and oedematous for 6 cm with a healed 18 cm surgical scar above.

skill.exam.surg.sinus_fistula_palpate.finding: Track firm and cord like, fixed to the underlying tibia which is broadened, irregular and tender along 10 cm. No mobility over deep structures. Left calf wasted by 3 cm compared with the right. No second opening, no crepitus.

skill.exam.surg.sinus_probing.finding: Probing deferred today: 6 cm of hot, red, tender cellulitis surrounds the opening with fever of 38.4 C, so the track will be probed gently under senior cover once the flare settles, with antibiotics on board. No joint communication assessed today.

skill.exam.surg.chronic_osteomyelitis.finding: Left tibia thickened and irregular from mid shaft downward with healed scarred puckering at the old wound. Ankle and knee movements full but painful at extremes. No shortening, no active deformity beyond the healed injury.

skill.exam.surg.regional_nodes.finding: Left inguinal nodes palpable, soft, tender, mobile, the largest 2 cm. Overlying skin normal and pinchable. Right groin and both axillae clear. No matted or stony hard node.

pus_culture.label: Pus microscopy, Gram stain, culture and sensitivity
pus_culture.result: Deep pus: Gram positive cocci in clusters on stain. Culture grows Staphylococcus aureus, sensitive to cloxacillin and first generation cephalosporins. No acid fast bacilli on stain.
pus_culture.note: Deep pus before antibiotics names the true pathogen; a skin edge swab would have grown colonisers. Sensitivity will narrow the empirical cover.

xray_leg.label: Plain radiograph of the left leg, two views
xray_leg.result: Dense linear sequestrum 5 cm long within a thick involucrum of the mid tibia, with two cloacae pointing to the skin. Intramedullary rod in situ with no loosening. No new fracture.
xray_leg.note: This is the keeper on film: dead bone inside living bone, draining through cloacae. It settles the diagnosis and mandates sequestrectomy, not more dressings.

cbc_esr.label: Complete blood count with ESR and CRP
cbc_esr.result: Haemoglobin 11.2 g per dL. Total leucocyte count 12,400 per cubic mm with 78 percent neutrophils. ESR 68 mm in the first hour. CRP raised.
cbc_esr.note: Anaemia of chronic disease with an acute on chronic leucocytosis and a high ESR: active flare on a chronic base. Tracks the response once the keeper is removed.

blood_sugar.label: Fasting blood sugar and HbA1c
blood_sugar.result: Fasting sugar 96 mg per dL. HbA1c 5.8 percent. No diabetes.
blood_sugar.note: Recurrent sepsis obliges a sugar check in every case; here it is normal, so poor control is not the keeper.

sinogram.label: Sinogram with radio opaque dye
sinogram.result: Deferred during the acute flare: not performed while spreading cellulitis and fever persist.
sinogram.note: Sinography is deferred until redness, heat and fever settle, since injecting dye into an acutely infected track risks spreading infection. The plain film already names the keeper, so reconsider mapping once the flare resolves, before surgery is planned.

chest_film.label: Chest radiograph
chest_film.result: Clear lung fields. No active or healed tuberculous lesion seen.
chest_film.note: A baseline before any operation and one more argument against a tuberculous keeper in this case.

mri_leg.label: Magnetic resonance imaging of the leg
mri_leg.note: Reserved for suspected joint spread, spinal involvement, or complex branching the plain film cannot map. Here the plain film already answers the surgical question, with sinography to follow once the flare settles if the surgeon needs the course mapped.

wound_biopsy.label: Edge biopsy
wound_biopsy.note: Indicated only for a raised, rolled or everted edge suspicious of Marjolin change. This edge sprouts granulation over infection, not tumour, so biopsy would add pain without information.

differentialModel.answer: Chronic osteomyelitis with a discharging sinus kept open by sequestrum. Consider tuberculous osteomyelitis, actinomycosis, cellulitis with a soft tissue abscess, necrotising fasciitis in the flare, an infected sebaceous cyst, and Marjolin change in the old scar.

diagnosis.answer: Chronic osteomyelitis of the left tibia with a discharging sinus, sequestrum in situ, currently in an acute infective flare.

managementModel.answer: Control the flare with culture guided antibiotics and analgesia, then admit for sequestrectomy with saucerisation and dependent drainage once fit, with sugar already checked, histopathology of removed tissue, and explicit return advice.

teachingPoints: Bony grit in the discharge is the diagnosis at the bedside: dead bone keeps this track open and no dressing dissolves it.
Sealing of the mouth followed by painful swelling proves a retained deep pool, not healing; each cycle scars the track further.
Sprouting granulation plus fixation to broadened tender tibia separates an osteomyelitic sinus from a tuberculous one with its blue undermined edge.
The probe striking a hard, gritty, moveable sequestrum names the keeper at the bedside; once the flare settles, a sinogram can prove the track is single and blind before surgery.
A normal sugar result is still a result: it removes diabetes from the keeper list and is recorded precisely for that reason.
The edge decides the biopsy, not the duration: granulation over infection needs surgery, while a raised everted edge needs histology first.
